name: Dar El Bacha
hero_subtitle: A 1910 pasha's palace, a museum of confluences and a very famous coffee house.

overview.title: The Pasha's House, Now a Museum
overview.p1: Dar El Bacha ('House of the Pasha') was built in 1910 as the residence of Thami El Glaoui, the powerful Pasha of Marrakech, and hosted figures such as Winston Churchill and Charlie Chaplin in its heyday. After decades of closure, it reopened in 2017 as the Museum of Confluences.
overview.p2: Inside, Islamic and African art sits alongside pieces reflecting Marrakech's Jewish heritage, among carved cedar doors, stained glass and zellige. One courtyard houses Bacha Coffee, now serving over 200 varieties of Arabica. Expect a wait for a table, and note that café access requires a museum ticket.

moods.title: What to See at Dar El Bacha
moods.subtitle: Architecture, art and coffee under one roof.

1.title: The Courtyards and Rooms
1.desc: Moorish architecture at its most polished, with carved cedar, zellige and stained glass throughout.

2.title: Museum of Confluences
2.desc: Islamic and African art alongside pieces from Marrakech's Jewish heritage, telling a story of exchange.

3.title: Bacha Coffee
3.desc: A historic coffee house with over 200 varieties of Arabica. Popular, so expect a wait and arrive early.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Dar El Bacha

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Dar El Bacha is in the medina, north of the Kasbah and west of the souks. Follow the signs from Jemaa el-Fnaa, or ask your riad for the simplest route.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Open daily except Monday, roughly 9:00 or 9:30 to 18:00 or 19:00. Go on a weekday morning to shorten the wait for Bacha Coffee.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: The museum ticket is around 70 MAD, and café access requires it. You order and pay separately inside for the coffee.

q1.question: Do I need a ticket to visit Bacha Coffee?
q1.answer: Yes. Access to the café requires a museum ticket, and you order and pay separately for your coffee.

q2.question: How long do you need at Dar El Bacha?
q2.answer: Plan on 1 to 2 hours, plus any wait for a table at Bacha Coffee.

q3.question: Which day is Dar El Bacha closed?
q3.answer: It is usually open daily except Monday. Hours can change, so check before you go.

q4.question: Who was the Pasha of Marrakech?
q4.answer: Thami El Glaoui, the powerful ruler of Marrakech who built the palace in 1910 and hosted famous guests there.
